reviews.frank_statement: Model/source output and textual capability references are proposals and never self-authorizing effects; effect authority is host/runtime controlled.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Capability metadata in ClayCode is sufficient and host/runtime resource enforcement is unnecessary.
reviews.falsifier: A reproducible untrusted execution path safely constrains effects using semantic metadata alone without host/runtime enforcement, including against forged/ambient access.
independent_checks: Current-run HTTP v2 execution denied missing/forged listener handles and executed only with a host-provided listener handle.
Parallel Linux sandbox experiment independently showed ordinary unsandboxed processes retain ambient filesystem authority and OS enforcement is required.
Official WIT/Component Model documentation independently models imported resources/interfaces as host-component boundaries rather than authority by textual name.
adversarial_checks: HTTP v1 token embedding was attacked by repeated execution and failed deterministic target identity.
HTTP v2 explicitly records that unrestricted Python is not itself a production capability sandbox.
reviews.reason: The core authority separation survives independent executable and external mechanism checks, while the concrete backend remains open.

reviews.frank_statement: No ambient OS authority; external effects should be mediated through host-minted effect permits/resources while preserving computational expressibility.
reviews.counterhypothesis: A conventional unrestricted process plus application-level checks is sufficient for ClayCode BASE and safer capability machinery can be deferred indefinitely.
reviews.falsifier: A complete adversarial application suite demonstrates no authority escape under unrestricted host APIs while preserving the same threat model.
independent_checks: Current-run inherited-listener experiment separates host bind authority from guest service behavior without embedding a secret into generated code.
Parallel Linux effect-boundary experiment produced a counterexample to metadata-only authority and positive namespace/resource-narrowing evidence.
adversarial_checks: The current Python target is intentionally classified as not sandbox-safe because arbitrary imports/host APIs could reintroduce ambient authority.
reviews.reason: The architectural rule is supported, but the concrete implementation should prefer opaque typed resource/handle imports plus OS/runtime enforcement; a raw FD in unrestricted Python is only a prototype mechanism.

reviews.frank_statement: Physical/backend encodings may be conventional as long as ClayCode remains the semantic source and crossings are typed/auditable rather than becoming a second semantic architecture.
reviews.counterhypothesis: A host HTTP adapter inevitably becomes a hidden second architecture and therefore HTTP must be a dedicated core ClayCode primitive.
reviews.falsifier: A realistic frozen APP-02 program cannot preserve route/state/effect semantics and receipts through a typed adapter without placing application semantics in backend-specific host code.
independent_checks: Current-run canonical IR lowered the same route/state semantics into deterministic generated host code without adding a ClayCode HTTP primitive.
Official Component Model/WIT design independently demonstrates typed interface/resource boundaries between semantic components and host functionality.
adversarial_checks: Streaming, async cancellation, structured errors, resource lifetimes and second-backend equivalence were not proven and remain explicit falsifiers.
reviews.reason: Typed FFI is sufficient for the bounded case, but a full APP-02/APP-04 differential test is required before treating the adapter design as release-ready.
